pathway.title: Diversified Healthcare Trust — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is high and has improved less than the headline suggests. Net debt was 8.84x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, down from 12.59x at 2025-12-31, but only 8.20x against 8.63x on the issuer's adjusted measure, because reported EBITDA carries impairments and gains on sale. Debt is flat at USD 2,404.05 million, so the gain came from earnings; the pro forma net leverage is 8.85x for the distribution declared on 2026-10-08 and 8.83x for the October 2026 reimbursement. Creditors carry a leverage level of about 8x to 9x with no debt paydown in 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M1; calculation M2; calculation M9

- Debt service is thin and cash generation is negative. Trailing cash interest cover is 1.34x, or 2.04x without the accreted interest of 2025, and free cash flow after real estate improvements was negative at USD 64.65 million over the last twelve months and negative at USD 12.11 million for nine months 2026 against USD 113.90 million a year earlier. Interest cost is mostly fixed, with 94.27% of principal at fixed rates, so the pressure is on earnings and capital spending rather than on rates; deleveraging therefore depends on net operating income growth and asset sales, not on retained cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 13–16, 53–54; calculation M1; calculation M6

- The earnings recovery is real and concentrated in senior housing. Quarterly net operating income of the managed senior housing portfolio rose to USD 49.66 million from USD 29.62 million, a rise of 67.66%, as margin on segment revenue went to 15.52% from 8.88% with occupancy at 83.8% against 81.5%. Each percentage point of that margin on annualised segment revenue is worth about USD 12.80 million, or 4.58% of trailing Adjusted EBITDAre, so the credit is highly sensitive to operating margin in one segment that produces 61.5% of net operating income. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 30–31, 46; calculation M4; calculation M7

- Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028 and liquidity does not cover it. Scheduled principal before 2028 is only USD 2.55 million, but USD 640.61 million falls due in 2028, made up of the senior unsecured notes due February 2028 and the floating rate mortgage loan due March 2028, against liquidity of USD 260.66 million, or 0.41x. If the USD 500.00 million of notes due February 2028 were refinanced at the 7.25% coupon of the 2030 secured notes, annual interest would rise by USD 12.50 million, which is 8.39% of the guided interest expense for 2026. The two 2025 financings moved the maturities out, but the runway ends in 2028. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation M3; calculation M5

- Access to the undrawn revolver is not established. The USD 150.00 million secured revolver matures in June 2029 and is available only subject to financial covenants and other conditions whose levels are not supplied, so liquidity of USD 260.66 million at 2026-09-30, before the events after that date, may be less usable than it looks; cash alone was USD 110.66 million, and pro forma cash for the post-quarter events is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 48–50

- Governance is manager-centred but behaviour has been benign. The external manager is controlled through the chair, its agreements run to 2045 with a termination fee of 19 years to 20 years of fees, and a cash incentive fee not tied to credit metrics is payable in January 2027 if earned; against that, no debt-funded payout or creditor-adverse transaction is documented and asset sales were applied to debt. The guided 2026 fee of USD 29.30 million is 26.48% of cash at 2026-09-30. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M8

- Ratings and market access are improving from a low base. Moody's upgraded the issuer to B3 with a positive outlook in April 2026 and S&P upgraded the senior unsecured notes to B and put the B- issuer rating on a positive outlook in October 2026; the 2025 refinancing was completed at a 7.25% coupon on the secured notes. Ratings come from the issuer's own text, no agency report is supplied, and the unsecured notes remain below the secured notes in rating. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, page 52; Source readiness (CP-0)

runs.text: The main strengths are the senior housing earnings recovery, light maturities before 2028 on mostly fixed-rate debt, asset-sale-funded debt reduction without shareholder payouts, a positive rating trajectory and an undrawn revolver. The recovery lifted segment net operating income by 67.66% and margin to 15.52%, which raises debt service capacity; only USD 2.55 million of principal falls due before 2028 and 94.27% of principal is fixed rate, which removes near-term refinancing and rate shocks; and the USD 510.08 million fall in debt in 2025 came from sale proceeds, not from new equity. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 13–16, 20, 30, 52; calculation M3; calculation M6; calculation M7

The main weaknesses are leverage of about 8x to 9x with cash interest cover of 1.34x, negative free cash flow, the 2028 maturity wall at more than twice liquidity, concentration in one segment and a few managers, and governance that rests on an external manager. Capital spending of USD 118.66 million exceeded operating cash flow, so no internal funds reduce debt; USD 640.61 million falls due in 2028; senior housing is 61.5% of net operating income and five managers hold 77.4% of book value; and the manager's agreements run to 2045 with a cash incentive fee not tied to credit metrics. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 16, 30; calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M13

cells.text: Diversified Healthcare Trust, a real estate investment trust organized under Maryland law in 1998; registrant of every periodic report

Owns senior living communities, medical office and life science properties and other healthcare real estate in 33 states and Washington, D.C.; 285 properties at 2026-09-30 (298 at 2025-12-31, 13 held for sale)
Senior housing operating portfolio (SHOP) and Medical Office and Life Science Portfolio; triple net leased senior living and wellness centers are reported as All Other
No employees; business and property management agreements with The RMR Group LLC, term to 2045 renewing annually; day to day operations are conducted by RMR
Communities are leased to taxable REIT subsidiaries and run by third-party managers under management agreements; 14 managers at 2025-12-31
Seven Trustees at 2025-12-31, five independent; the Chair is a Managing Trustee
ABP Trust and Mr. Portnoy owned 9.8% of common shares at 2026-09-30; ABP Trust controls RMR Inc., the parent of the manager
Deloitte and Touche LLP gave unqualified opinions on the 2025 financial statements and on internal control over financial reporting
Common shares and two series of listed senior notes trade on Nasdaq; 242,529,157 common shares outstanding at 2026-10-30
Moody's B3 with a positive outlook (April 2026); S&P B- issuer rating with a positive outlook (October 2026)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The trust's recent transactions are refinancings and disposals, not an acquisition or a sponsor-led deal. In 2025 it sold 69 properties for USD 604.87 million, applied USD 402.23 million of net proceeds to partly redeem the senior secured notes due 2026, and redeemed the remainder in full by 2025-12-29, having paid USD 152.87 million of accreted interest in cash during the year. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 185, 197, 221; calculation K5

The new debt of 2025 was USD 375.00 million of 7.25% senior secured notes due 2030, issued in September 2025 with net proceeds of USD 364.73 million and secured by a first-priority lien on the equity of subsidiaries that own 36 properties; four mortgage financings totalling USD 343.16 million between March and May 2025 secured on 14, 7, 4 and 2 senior housing communities; and a USD 150.00 million secured revolver obtained in June 2025 that was undrawn at 2026-09-30. The notes mature in 2030 and the mortgage loans between 2028 and 2035, which moved the nearest large maturity to 2028. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 220, 222–224; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, page 16

No debt was issued in the first nine months of 2026. The transactions of that period are the sale of 13 communities for USD 23.00 million in March 2026 and the USD 14.50 million purchase of two land parcels in April 2026 that ended two finance leases. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 7

fields.value: The ten filings and releases support a credit snapshot of Diversified Healthcare Trust as of 2026-11-18 with limitations: statements, debt, liquidity and segments are sourced to 2026-09-30, but covenant levels and executed debt documents are absent, and EBITDA appears only as management non-GAAP figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors can rely on the audited 2024 and 2025 statements and the three 2026 quarterly reports for debt, maturities and revolver availability. Covenant headroom, recovery, market pricing and peer comparison cannot be assessed from this set. Quarterly earnings measures such as EBITDAre come only from the investor presentations, and their definition changed in the third quarter of 2026. The November 2026 presentation also carries two sets of liquidity figures, and the set that matches the quarterly report is the one used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 16, 44; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 20–21; calculation C1; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each check below uses only figures printed in the sources. Amounts are in thousands of US dollars unless a cell says otherwise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Executed debt documents are not supplied. The run settings declare no legal documents, and the filings only summarize the credit agreement, indentures and mortgage loan agreements and list the indentures in their exhibit indexes. Covenant levels, definitions, step-downs and headroom are therefore not established; the filings state only that the trust believed it was in compliance at 2026-09-30. This limits the covenant view in Fundamental credit and would block Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity and Recovery & fulcrum if requested. Severity: material.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The filings print no EBITDA, EBITDAre or net debt. Quarterly EBITDA, EBITDAre and Adjusted EBITDAre come only from the investor presentations, which are management documents: the November 2026 presentation covers the five quarters to 2026-09-30 on the revised definition that includes incentive management fees, and the May 2026 presentation covers the five quarters to 2026-03-31 on the earlier definition. First-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDAre is therefore USD 74,004 thousand as first presented and USD 67,376 thousand recast, and Normalized FFO is USD 33,098 thousand against USD 26,470 thousand. The net debt amount and the interest coverage inputs behind the issuer's stated leverage of 8.2x and coverage of 2.0x are not printed, and the quarterly financial supplements that the news releases point to by web link are not supplied. Severity: minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, page 44; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 20, 21; EX99.1_2026-03-31_dhc_tm2613539d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The November 2026 presentation's debt slide carries two sets of figures. The updated set shows near-term available liquidity of $260.7 Million, fixed rate debt of 94.3% and unencumbered assets of $4.0 Billion; the other set shows $271.8 Million, 94.2% and $4.2 Billion and reads word for word like the first set on the May 2026 presentation's slide as of March 31, 2026. The quarterly report supports the updated liquidity figure and the other liquidity figure equals the March 31, 2026 balance, so liquidity is settled; the quarterly report prints no unencumbered asset total, so the choice between $4.0 Billion and $4.2 Billion is not established, and the fixed rate share must be recomputed from the debt table. Severity: minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX99.1_2026-03-31_dhc_tm2613539d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The definitive proxy statement is not supplied. The annual report gives the board's size and independence and its governance provisions, but incorporates committee membership, independence determinations, executive compensation and related-transaction detail from the proxy statement, so governance is read from the annual report and the related-person notes only. Severity: minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The full year 2026 guidance release of 2026-06-01 and the earnings call materials are not supplied. The November 2026 presentation shows a previous guidance column without a date, and the May 2026 presentation restates the guidance issued on 2026-02-23, so the 2026 guidance history is rebuilt from those two presentations only. Severity: minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - There is no standalone report or release for the fourth quarter of 2025. The two presentations reconcile that quarter's net loss to NOI, EBITDAre and Normalized FFO, but its other statement lines can only be derived as the full year 2025 less the nine months of 2025 shown in the third quarter 2026 report. Cash interest paid for 2025 also includes accreted interest on the former secured notes, so it is not comparable with 2026 cash interest. Severity: minor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No rating agency report, market quote, peer filing or portfolio file is supplied, and the run settings leave each empty. Ratings facts therefore come from the issuer's own text, and peer comparison, market-implied risk and portfolio fit cannot be assessed. Severity: minor for this pathway.

fields.value: Diversified Healthcare Trust (dhc-1075415), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the Financial foundation of the trust's consolidated statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the ten supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage remains high and has improved less than reported EBITDA implies: net debt was 8.84x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 12.59x at 2025-12-31, but 8.20x against 8.63x on the issuer's adjusted measure, with debt flat, so creditors still depend on earnings growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Total debt at carrying value was USD 2,404.05 million, net debt fell by only USD 2.02 million since 2025-12-31 and trailing free cash flow was negative at USD 64.65 million. Liquidity of USD 260.66 million covers the USD 2.55 million of scheduled principal before 2028 many times but only 0.41x of the USD 640.61 million due in 2028. Trailing cash interest cover was 1.34x, or 2.04x excluding accreted interest paid in 2025. Net leverage of 8.84x is 8.85x pro forma for the distribution declared on 2026-10-08 and 8.83x pro forma for the reimbursement received from the LSMD joint venture in October 2026. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is not established.

Amounts are USD thousands as the filing prints them; carrying values are printed for groups of instruments only, so each instrument's principal is its Reporting Currency Amount and one financing cost adjustment row reconciles to Total Debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt to reported EBITDA fell from 18.39x at 2024-12-31 to 12.59x at 2025-12-31 and 8.84x at 2026-09-30, but the two steps have different causes. In 2025 total debt at carrying value fell by USD 510.08 million, as USD 589.23 million of property sale proceeds, USD 343.16 million of new mortgage financings and USD 369.38 million of new senior secured notes were applied to redeem USD 750.00 million of senior secured notes and USD 380.00 million of senior unsecured notes, so the first step was real deleveraging, funded mainly by property sales. Since 2025-12-31 total debt has risen by USD 3.23 million and net debt has fallen by only USD 2.02 million, so the second step came entirely from trailing reported EBITDA rising by USD 77.21 million to USD 259.49 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, page 177; 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 182, 184; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K6; calculation K19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: That rise overstates the operating improvement, because reported EBITDA is struck after impairments and includes gains on sale. The 2025 figure carries an impairment of USD 165.70 million and a gain on sale of USD 117.73 million, while the trailing twelve months carry impairments of USD 17.54 million and a net gain on sale of USD 11.03 million. On the issuer's adjusted measure, which removes those items and deducts incentive management fees, net debt to trailing earnings moved only from 8.63x to 8.20x, because Adjusted EBITDAre rose by USD 13.53 million, from USD 266.08 million to USD 279.61 million. The creditor consequence is that leverage of about 8x to 9x is the fair description of the capital structure today, and that further deleveraging needs higher earnings or asset sale proceeds applied to debt, since free cash flow is negative.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, page 183; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation K5; calculation K6; calculation K9; calculation K15; calculation K19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The driver of the earnings gain is the senior housing operating portfolio. Its quarterly net operating income rose from USD 29.62 million in Q3 2025 to USD 49.66 million in Q3 2026, a rise of 67.66%, with occupancy across all properties of 83.8% against 81.5% and an average monthly rate of USD 5,670 per occupied unit against USD 5,472. The segment is now 61.49% of net operating income, so debt service increasingly depends on operator performance in one segment, while medical office and life science net operating income fell from USD 26.68 million to USD 23.87 million over the same year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest cover on reported EBITDA was 1.14x for 2024, 0.67x for 2025 and 1.34x for the twelve months to 2026-09-30. The 2025 and trailing figures are depressed by accreted interest paid in cash when the zero-coupon senior secured notes due 2026 were redeemed: USD 152.87 million in 2025, of which USD 65.88 million fell in the fourth quarter and so sits inside the trailing window. Excluding it, cover was 1.53x for 2025 and 2.04x trailing, and the issuer's own 2.0x is reproduced as Adjusted EBITDAre over interest expense less non-cash amortization at 2.01x. Creditors should read run-rate cover as about 2x, with the lower trailing figure reflecting a one-off cash cost that leaves the window with the fourth quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 183, 185; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 5, 47; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 22; calculation K8; calculation K10; calculation K11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The interest burden is largely fixed: 94.27% of principal is at fixed rates, in line with the 94.3% the issuer states, and the only floating exposure is the USD 140.00 million mortgage loan, whose 4.50% SOFR cap runs to March 2027, a year before the loan's March 2028 maturity. Rate moves therefore matter for refinancing in 2028 more than for current interest cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 54.01 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 against real estate improvements of USD 118.66 million, so free cash flow was negative at USD 64.65 million. The nine months to 2026-09-30 were less negative at USD 12.11 million against USD 113.90 million a year earlier, mainly because interest paid fell once accreted interest of USD 86.99 million stopped. The 2026 shortfall was more than covered by a USD 27.20 million dividend from AlerisLife and USD 21.69 million of sale proceeds, not by borrowing, and cash rose by USD 5.25 million to USD 110.66 million. The consequence is that no free cash flow is available to repay debt, so the maturity wall in 2028 must be refinanced or met from asset sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 184–185; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 47; calculation K6; calculation K19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Working capital helped the nine months: other assets released USD 21.00 million while other liabilities used USD 17.10 million, including the USD 17.91 million incentive management fee for 2025 paid to the manager in January 2026. Capital spending can be deferred, since the issuer states that it may defer certain redevelopment projects to preserve liquidity, and it reports recurring capital expenditure of USD 67.80 million for the nine months within the USD 86.22 million of real estate improvements, but the statements give no maintenance and growth split.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity was USD 260.66 million: cash of USD 110.66 million plus the undrawn USD 150.00 million revolver, with restricted cash of USD 20.29 million excluded. Scheduled principal before 2028 is only USD 2.55 million, so near-term refinancing risk is low, but USD 640.61 million falls due in 2028, made up of USD 500.00 million of senior unsecured notes due February 2028 and the USD 140.00 million floating rate mortgage loan with two one-year extension options. Liquidity covers 0.41x of that wall, and the revolver is secured on 14 senior living communities and available only subject to covenants and conditions whose levels are not supplied, so the wall rests on asset sales, refinancing or earnings growth rather than on liquidity on hand. An incentive management fee for 2026, if earned, is payable to the manager in January 2027; USD 22.00 million had been recognised by 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 16, 23, 47–49; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation K13; calculation K17; calculation K19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is the pace of the senior housing recovery and the direction of the ratings. Quarterly SHOP net operating income rose in each quarter from Q3 2025 to Q2 2026 and eased by USD 3.83 million in Q3 2026; Moody's upgraded the issuer to B3 with a positive outlook in April 2026, and S&P raised its senior unsecured rating to B and put the B- issuer rating on a positive outlook in October 2026. Annualising the Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDAre of USD 73.42 million gives net leverage of 7.81x, and management targets 5.5x to 6.5x excluding incentive fees. That view would win if Adjusted EBITDAre holds at the Q3 2026 run rate with net debt flat, or if sale proceeds are applied to debt; it would lose if occupancy reverses or the 2028 maturities are refinanced at a higher cost.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA is derived from the statements because no filing prints it, and the Adjusted EBITDAre definition changed in Q3 2026 to deduct incentive management fees. One event therefore has two figures: Q1 2026 Adjusted EBITDAre was USD 74.00 million as first presented in May 2026 and USD 67.38 million as recast, the difference being the incentive fee of USD 6.63 million. The recast figure serves every trailing and ratio calculation, because it is comparable across the five quarters. The issuer's leverage of 7.8x in the May presentation is on the earlier definition and is not reproduced by the same construction, which gives 8.06x, so it is not used. Reported EBITDA of USD 259.49 million and Adjusted EBITDAre of USD 279.61 million are both shown so that the reader can see how much of the gap between them is impairment and gains on sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Outside the debt figure the trust has a limited recourse guaranty of up to USD 100.00 million on USD 1,000.00 million of secured debt at the Seaport joint venture, lessee lease liabilities of USD 14.17 million inside other liabilities, unspent leasing obligations of USD 11.01 million expected to be spent within twelve months, and the estimated 2026 incentive management fee. The debt of the LSMD joint venture is non-recourse to the trust, and the annual report states that the trust is party to no litigation it expects to have a material adverse effect. No pensions, retiree medical obligations, factoring, supply chain finance, purchase commitments, letters of credit or consent decrees were found in any of the ten sources, and no customer deposits or deferred revenue are itemised as a funding float; other liabilities of USD 230.52 million are not broken down in the quarterly report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Several events follow the balance sheet date and are kept out of period figures. A distribution of USD 2.43 million was declared on 2026-10-08 for payment around 2026-11-12, which would raise net debt to USD 2,295.82 million and net leverage to 8.85x; the LSMD joint venture reimbursed USD 1.22 million in October 2026, which would lower net debt to USD 2,292.17 million; a vacant medical office property was under agreement to be sold for USD 10.50 million on 2026-11-02 and had not closed; and on 2026-10-01 seven skilled nursing facilities moved from management agreements to a triple net lease. They are excluded from period figures because they fall after the balance sheet date, and the pro forma figures are in the adjustments table.

A search of all ten sources found no letters of credit, standby facilities, pensions, retiree medical obligations, factoring, supply chain finance, purchase commitments or consent decrees; the trust has no employees and is party to no litigation it expects to be material. Severity: Medium. Action: monitor the January 2027 fee payment and any call on the Seaport guaranty.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diversified Healthcare Trust (dhc-1075415), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, ownership, management and governance facts, transactions and operating model behind the credit, from the ten supplied filings and releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance risk is moderate and structural rather than behavioural: an external manager controlled by the trust's chair runs the company, and 61.5% of net operating income rests on third-party senior housing operators, yet no debt-funded payout or creditor-adverse transaction is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The manager's agreements run to 2045 and renew each year, and ending them for convenience would cost a fee equal to the present value of 19 years to 20 years of future fees. The trust paid the manager a cash incentive fee of USD 17.91 million for 2025 and has recognised USD 22.00 million for the first nine months of 2026, while it pays shareholders only USD 0.01 per share a quarter and applied 2025 property sale proceeds to debt. The debt documents, covenant levels and proxy statement are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control sits with the manager, not with creditors or an independent owner. Every officer of the trust is an officer and employee of the manager, the trust's chair controls the manager's parent through ABP Trust, and the trust has no employees; five of seven Trustees were independent at 2025-12-31. The agreements run to 2045, ending them for convenience on 60 days notice would cost a fee equal to 19 years to 20 years of future fees, or the fee for 10 years if the reason is performance, and in January 2025 the trust consented to the pledge of the manager's rights to the manager's lender and agreed to give that lender 30 days to cure a manager default before it terminates. For creditors this means that independent Trustees, not owner incentives, are the check on related-party decisions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating risk is concentrated in one segment run by outside operators. Senior housing operations produce 61.5% of net operating income and 87.01% of revenues; the largest manager holds communities worth 30.5% of gross real estate book value and the three largest hold 63.1%. Managers of roughly half the managed communities were replaced between September 2025 and December 2025 when the related operator AlerisLife wound down, and notice was given on six more communities in September 2026, so results depend on how those transitions bed in. Occupancy across all senior housing properties rose to 83.8% from 81.5% and quarterly net operating income to USD 49.66 million from USD 29.62 million, which is the evidence for the recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 20, 30–31, 46; calculation K3; calculation K4; calculation K11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation has favoured creditors so far. In 2025 the trust sold 69 properties for USD 604.87 million and applied USD 402.23 million of net proceeds to redeem secured notes; it acquired no property in 2023, 2024 or 2025; it holds its distribution at USD 0.01 per share a quarter, USD 9.66 million for 2025; and it issued no debt in 2026 to 2026-09-30. No dividend recapitalisation, priming, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange is described in the sources read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash leakage to the manager is moderate, but it is paid in cash on a formula that ignores credit metrics. The trust paid the manager USD 52.74 million in 2025 and USD 47.59 million in the first nine months of 2026, of which incentive fees were USD 17.91 million and USD 22.00 million. The fee is 12.0% of equity market capitalisation times the amount by which three-year total return exceeds an index, capped at 1.5% of shares, so a positive share return, not leverage or free cash flow, triggers payment; management guidance puts the 2026 fee at USD 29.30 million, payable in January 2027, which is 26.48% of cash at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 211–214; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 23–24; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation K1; calculation K2; calculation K10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No creditor-adverse behaviour is documented, but legal capacity is not established. Willingness evidence is benign: small distributions, property sales applied to debt and redemptions at principal. Capacity under restricted payment, investment, lien and guarantee-release terms cannot be assessed because the debt documents are not supplied. The 2025 refinancing added secured debt, yet the secured share of principal was 34.46% at 2026-09-30 against 35.09% at 2024-12-31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Disclosure supports monitoring of the financial statements but not of covenants. Audit opinions on the 2025 statements and on internal control were unqualified and disclosure controls were effective at 2026-09-30, but covenant levels are not printed and governance detail is incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a higher risk level is the manager's contractual entrenchment: terms to 2045, a termination fee of 19 years to 20 years of fees, a cash incentive fee that is paid regardless of credit metrics, and a pledge consent that delays any termination by 30 days. The strongest evidence for a lower level is conduct: no debt-funded payout, asset sales applied to debt, redemptions at principal and a board with five independent Trustees out of seven whose Independent Trustees approved the pledge consent. The view would move higher if the debt documents give wide restricted payment, investment or guarantee-release capacity, if the trust funds a distribution or related-party transfer with debt, or if the proxy statement shows that independent Trustees do not control the committees that approve related-party matters. It would move lower if the documents restrict payments tightly and the termination fee proves small. A lender call on the manager's pledge, or an incentive fee payable in January 2027 that exceeds the guided amount, would also weigh on the view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so committee membership, independence determinations and the ownership table are not established; the board-independence part of the first finding rests on the annual report's count of five independent Trustees out of seven, and the other shareholders cannot be named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The credit agreement, indentures and mortgage loan agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, further secured debt, investments and the release of guarantees is not established; the risk level describes documented behaviour only and would rise if the documents grant wide capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No statements are supplied for the manager, its parent, ABP Trust or AlerisLife, so the manager's own strength behind its lender pledge and the residual value of the AlerisLife wind-down are not established; the entrenchment finding is therefore read from contract terms alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2026 incentive fee estimate is a management figure from the November 2026 presentation, which does not reconcile its guidance to GAAP; it sizes the January 2027 cash call but is not a contractual amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trust's recent transactions are refinancings and disposals, not an acquisition or a sponsor-led deal. In 2025 it sold 69 properties for USD 604.87 million, applied USD 402.23 million of net proceeds to partly redeem the senior secured notes due 2026, and redeemed the remainder in full by 2025-12-29, having paid USD 152.87 million of accreted interest in cash during the year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The new debt of 2025 was USD 375.00 million of 7.25% senior secured notes due 2030, issued in September 2025 with net proceeds of USD 364.73 million and secured by a first-priority lien on the equity of subsidiaries that own 36 properties; four mortgage financings totalling USD 343.16 million between March and May 2025 secured on 14, 7, 4 and 2 senior housing communities; and a USD 150.00 million secured revolver obtained in June 2025 that was undrawn at 2026-09-30. The notes mature in 2030 and the mortgage loans between 2028 and 2035, which moved the nearest large maturity to 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No debt was issued in the first nine months of 2026. The transactions of that period are the sale of 13 communities for USD 23.00 million in March 2026 and the USD 14.50 million purchase of two land parcels in April 2026 that ended two finance leases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The registers below carry the method's tables in full. Registers the transport does not ask for are not written.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by the manager's control of the trust and its long contracts, because the party that runs the trust is also the counterparty to its fee contracts, which implies weak creditor leverage over related-party decisions. Countervailing evidence is that independent Trustees approved the pledge consent and that distributions, asset sales and redemptions have all favoured creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The absorbed governance assessment is completed with limitations. Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. Key gaps: the debt documents, the covenant levels and the proxy statement.

Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting.

fields.value: - The credit agreement, indentures and mortgage loan agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity for restricted payments, investments, liens, guarantee releases, priming and amendments is not established and the risk level rests on documented behaviour alone. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed credit agreement and indentures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant levels, definitions, step-downs and headroom are not printed; the trust states only that it believed it was in compliance at 2026-09-30, so the usability of the undrawn revolver cannot be tested. Severity: High. Action: obtain compliance certificates or the financing documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The dollar amount of the termination fee under the manager's agreements is not supplied; the filings give only the formula of 19 years to 20 years of future fees, so the contingent cost of changing manager cannot be sized. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the management agreements and the manager's fee calculation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No financial statements are supplied for the manager, its parent, ABP Trust or AlerisLife, so the strength of the manager behind its lender pledge and the residual of the AlerisLife wind-down are not established. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the parent's filings and wind-down information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The cost of the operator changes, including the termination fees on six communities and the transition to the Ensign lease, is not quantified. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the fourth quarter 2026 report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management statements in the investor presentations, including total shareholder return, growth claims and the estimated 2026 incentive fee, are management language and are not reconciled to GAAP; they are used only to size the January 2027 fee and are not relied on elsewhere. Severity: Low. Action: none beyond the quarterly supplements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Seasonality of operating metrics is not stated in the sources, so quarter to quarter changes in senior housing net operating income, such as the fall from the second to the third quarter of 2026, cannot be separated from trend. Severity: Low. Action: compare like quarters in later reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diversified Healthcare Trust (dhc-1075415), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated fundamental credit synthesis, drawing on the supplied filings, releases and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance handoffs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is weak but improving: senior housing earnings gains cut adjusted net leverage to 8.20x, yet debt is flat, free cash flow is negative and USD 640.61 million falls due in 2028, so creditors depend on continued operating gains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 13–16, 30; calculation M1; calculation M3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trailing cash interest cover is thin at 1.34x, or 2.04x excluding accreted interest paid in 2025, and liquidity of USD 260.66 million covers 0.41x of the 2028 maturities. Reported net leverage is 8.84x at 2026-09-30, 8.85x pro forma for the distribution declared on 2026-10-08 and 8.83x pro forma for the reimbursement received in October 2026. The debt is mostly fixed rate, the nearest large maturity is 2028 and the ratings are on positive outlook, which buys time but no cushion. Covenant levels are not supplied, so access to the undrawn USD 150.00 million revolver is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 20, 26, 52; calculation M1; calculation M2; calculation M3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is high and has improved less than the headline suggests. Net debt was 8.84x trailing reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, down from 12.59x at 2025-12-31, but only 8.20x against 8.63x on the issuer's adjusted measure, because reported EBITDA carries impairments and gains on sale. Debt is flat at USD 2,404.05 million, so the gain came from earnings; the pro forma net leverage is 8.85x for the distribution declared on 2026-10-08 and 8.83x for the October 2026 reimbursement. Creditors carry a leverage level of about 8x to 9x with no debt paydown in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M1; calculation M2; calculation M9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt service is thin and cash generation is negative. Trailing cash interest cover is 1.34x, or 2.04x without the accreted interest of 2025, and free cash flow after real estate improvements was negative at USD 64.65 million over the last twelve months and negative at USD 12.11 million for nine months 2026 against USD 113.90 million a year earlier. Interest cost is mostly fixed, with 94.27% of principal at fixed rates, so the pressure is on earnings and capital spending rather than on rates; deleveraging therefore depends on net operating income growth and asset sales, not on retained cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 13–16, 53–54; calculation M1; calculation M6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The earnings recovery is real and concentrated in senior housing. Quarterly net operating income of the managed senior housing portfolio rose to USD 49.66 million from USD 29.62 million, a rise of 67.66%, as margin on segment revenue went to 15.52% from 8.88% with occupancy at 83.8% against 81.5%. Each percentage point of that margin on annualised segment revenue is worth about USD 12.80 million, or 4.58% of trailing Adjusted EBITDAre, so the credit is highly sensitive to operating margin in one segment that produces 61.5% of net operating income.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 30–31, 46; calculation M4; calculation M7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028 and liquidity does not cover it. Scheduled principal before 2028 is only USD 2.55 million, but USD 640.61 million falls due in 2028, made up of the senior unsecured notes due February 2028 and the floating rate mortgage loan due March 2028, against liquidity of USD 260.66 million, or 0.41x. If the USD 500.00 million of notes due February 2028 were refinanced at the 7.25% coupon of the 2030 secured notes, annual interest would rise by USD 12.50 million, which is 8.39% of the guided interest expense for 2026. The two 2025 financings moved the maturities out, but the runway ends in 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation M3; calculation M5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Access to the undrawn revolver is not established. The USD 150.00 million secured revolver matures in June 2029 and is available only subject to financial covenants and other conditions whose levels are not supplied, so liquidity of USD 260.66 million at 2026-09-30, before the events after that date, may be less usable than it looks; cash alone was USD 110.66 million, and pro forma cash for the post-quarter events is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Governance is manager-centred but behaviour has been benign. The external manager is controlled through the chair, its agreements run to 2045 with a termination fee of 19 years to 20 years of fees, and a cash incentive fee not tied to credit metrics is payable in January 2027 if earned; against that, no debt-funded payout or creditor-adverse transaction is documented and asset sales were applied to debt. The guided 2026 fee of USD 29.30 million is 26.48% of cash at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ratings and market access are improving from a low base. Moody's upgraded the issuer to B3 with a positive outlook in April 2026 and S&P upgraded the senior unsecured notes to B and put the B- issuer rating on a positive outlook in October 2026; the 2025 refinancing was completed at a 7.25% coupon on the secured notes. Ratings come from the issuer's own text, no agency report is supplied, and the unsecured notes remain below the secured notes in rating.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a better credit view is the pace and breadth of the recovery: quarterly senior housing net operating income up 67.66%, two rating upgrades, a 2025 refinancing that moved maturities to 2028 and beyond, debt that is mostly fixed rate, and management's own target of 5.5x to 6.5x leverage excluding incentive fees. Annualising the third quarter of 2026 Adjusted EBITDAre of USD 73.42 million would give net leverage of 7.81x. That view would win if Adjusted EBITDAre holds at the third-quarter run rate for several quarters, if asset sale proceeds or retained cash are applied to debt, and if the 2028 maturities are refinanced before they fall within twelve months. It would fail if senior housing occupancy or margin reverses, since one percentage point of margin is about USD 12.80 million of earnings, if the operator transitions disrupt results, or if refinancing is only available at coupons near the 7.25% of the 2030 secured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main strengths are the senior housing earnings recovery, light maturities before 2028 on mostly fixed-rate debt, asset-sale-funded debt reduction without shareholder payouts, a positive rating trajectory and an undrawn revolver. The recovery lifted segment net operating income by 67.66% and margin to 15.52%, which raises debt service capacity; only USD 2.55 million of principal falls due before 2028 and 94.27% of principal is fixed rate, which removes near-term refinancing and rate shocks; and the USD 510.08 million fall in debt in 2025 came from sale proceeds, not from new equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weaknesses are leverage of about 8x to 9x with cash interest cover of 1.34x, negative free cash flow, the 2028 maturity wall at more than twice liquidity, concentration in one segment and a few managers, and governance that rests on an external manager. Capital spending of USD 118.66 million exceeded operating cash flow, so no internal funds reduce debt; USD 640.61 million falls due in 2028; senior housing is 61.5% of net operating income and five managers hold 77.4% of book value; and the manager's agreements run to 2045 with a cash incentive fee not tied to credit metrics.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 16, 30; calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diversified Healthcare Trust is a Maryland healthcare REIT that earns income in two ways. Managed senior living communities are leased to its own taxable subsidiaries and run by third-party managers for a fee, and medical office and life science properties are let to tenants under net, modified gross and full-service leases; a small book of triple net leased senior living and wellness properties adds contractual rent. Revenue in the larger segment is residents' fees that move with occupancy and rate, so cash flow visibility is lower than for a net lease REIT and operating leverage is high. The portfolio changed in 2025, when 69 properties were sold and the medical office base shrank; senior housing now produces 87.01% of revenue and 61.5% of net operating income, which ties debt service to operator performance in one segment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 30; calculation M7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trust is a public REIT with no sponsor fund and no equity cure behind it. ABP Trust and the chair hold 9.8% of the shares and control the parent of the external manager, which employs every officer and holds agreements to 2045 with a termination fee of 19 years to 20 years of fees, so governance leverage for creditors rests on independent Trustees. Debt sits at the parent and at property-owning subsidiaries: the 4.375% notes due 2031 carry unsecured subsidiary guarantees, the 7.25% notes due 2030 are secured on the equity of subsidiaries owning 36 properties, and the other three unsecured series carry no guarantee, so they rank behind USD 841.40 million of secured principal and behind the creditors of subsidiaries. Financial policy has been conservative in conduct: small distributions, no acquisitions in 2023, 2024 or 2025, and property sales applied to debt; detailed ranking and legal capacity belong to Structural priority and Legal & covenants, for which the debt documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Residents' fees are 91.11% basic housing and support services paid privately and 6.40% from Medicare and Medicaid, so volume and rate drive revenue and government reimbursement is a small exposure. Occupancy across all senior housing properties was 83.8% in Q3 2026 against 81.5% a year earlier and the average monthly rate was USD 5,670 against USD 5,472, a rise of 3.62%, so rate has carried part of the gain. The trust cites constrained supply, with inventory growth of 0.5% and absorption of 2.8% in the fourth quarter of 2025 from a third-party source, which supports occupancy but is a management reading. Medical office and life science revenue is contractual but shrinking, at USD 40.40 million against USD 48.20 million in Q3, with 20.3% of annualized rental income expiring in 2028 and a weighted average remaining term of 4.9 years; new and renewal leases in Q3 2026 were signed at a rental rate change of 25.2%. Revenue is recurring in form, cyclical in occupancy and concentrated in one segment, and the filings describe no long-term contract protection for resident revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 31–33; 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; calculation M11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs follow the operation of the communities and sit with the managers: labor and benefits were 48.18% of segment revenue in Q3 2026 against 51.72% a year earlier and management fees 5.68% against 5.31%, with insurance, utilities and food the other named pressures. Net operating income margin rose to 15.52% from 8.88% and part of that gain reflects a smaller portfolio, since units fell from 24,906 to 22,445, so the margin is both an improvement and a base for operating deleverage. Management fees move with revenue and incentive fees share the upside above target EBITDA, so lenders bear the downside. The issuer expects labor, insurance and food cost increases to moderate, which is a management view; margins can be defended under modest volume pressure but not under a combined wage and occupancy shock.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 20, 30–31; 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation M4; calculation M12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is high against cash earnings. Real estate improvements were USD 118.66 million over the last twelve months against operating cash flow of USD 54.01 million, so free cash flow after interest was negative at USD 64.65 million, and EBITDA does not convert to free cash flow available for debt reduction. Recurring capital expenditure, the issuer's non-GAAP figure, was USD 67.80 million for nine months 2026 against USD 96.38 million, and the issuer guides USD 90.00 million to USD 105.00 million for 2026; the trust says it may defer certain redevelopment projects to preserve liquidity, which is a lever, and cash taxes are small at USD 3.18 million for nine months. Cash interest of USD 193.02 million over the last twelve months includes USD 65.88 million of accreted interest paid in the fourth quarter of 2025, which will not recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 8, 47–48; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dhc_tm2629915d1-ex99-1-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 22; calculation M1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry matters through occupancy: senior housing competes community by community, and supply growth is low at 0.5% a year in the trust's cited data, which limits the pressure on occupancy and rate. The threat of new entrants is restrained by the cost of financing and construction, which the annual report names as the reason supply has stayed low, so competitors cannot quickly add units and dilute pricing. Buyer power is moderate: residents pay mostly privately and monthly rates rose 3.62% in a year, while medical office tenants renewed at higher rents, so there is no evidence of pricing pressure; the threat of substitutes, such as home care, is not established in the sources. Supplier power is the weaker side: labor is the largest cost line at 48.18% of segment revenue and the trust relies on managers that set rents and hire staff, so wage inflation and manager performance are the forces that most affect margin and cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 11–12, 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 30–32; calculation M11; calculation M12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PEST factors are only partly a primary credit driver. Regulatory exposure is small, because Medicare and Medicaid are 6.40% of residents' fees and only a small amount of net operating income comes from properties that depend mainly on them; economic factors matter more, through labor inflation, interest rates and the financing market that sets the cost of refinancing the 2028 maturities; the social factor, a growing population aged 75 and over at about 4% a year between 2025 and 2035 on the trust's cited census projection, supports demand; technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver in the materials provided.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: senior housing net operating income up 67.66% in a year; no scheduled principal of note before 2028; 94.27% of principal at fixed rates; asset sales that reduced debt without distributions; rating upgrades. Weaknesses: net leverage of about 8x to 9x; cash interest cover of 1.34x; negative free cash flow; concentration in one segment and in a few managers; governance that depends on an externally managed structure. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: further occupancy and margin gains toward the market levels the issuer cites, sale proceeds applied to debt, and refinancing of the 2028 maturities early. Threats that could weaken it: wage and insurance inflation, operator transitions on six communities and on the Ensign lease, manager failure, revolver access limited by covenants, and refinancing at a higher coupon.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 30, 52; calculation M1; calculation M4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average: gross real estate book value is USD 6,274.29 million across the portfolio, large enough to absorb disposals, but no market share data is supplied. Competitive advantage is not assessable: no peer or market data is supplied and operations are outsourced. Business diversification is average: five managers hold 77.4% of gross real estate book value and the segment is 61.5% of net operating income, but the properties sit in 33 states. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital spending can be deferred, but labor is 48.18% of segment revenue. Margin stability is weak: segment margin rose from 8.88% to 15.52% in a year, which shows how far it can swing. Free cash flow stability is weak: free cash flow was negative at USD 89.48 million for 2024, USD 166.44 million for 2025 and USD 64.65 million trailing. Ability to refinance is average and improving: the 2025 refinancing worked and ratings rose, but USD 640.61 million falls due in 2028. Liquidity position is average: USD 260.66 million covers near-term maturities many times but only 0.41x of 2028, and covenant headroom is not established. Financial policy and governance is average: behaviour is benign, but control sits with the external manager. The main supports are the earnings recovery, the maturity profile to 2028 and conservative financial policy; the main constraints are leverage, thin cover and negative free cash flow; the trend is improving; the missing datapoints are covenant levels, peer data and the proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 20, 30–31; calculation M1; calculation M3; calculation M13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the issuer guides 2026 Adjusted EBITDAre of USD 275.70 million to USD 290.70 million and interest expense of USD 149.00 million, which would give cover of about 1.90x on guidance, a management view not reconciled to GAAP. Tailwinds are senior housing occupancy and rate momentum, constrained supply, a lease with Ensign that converts seven skilled nursing facilities to contractual rent from 2026-10-01, and fixed-rate debt. Headwinds are labor and insurance costs, the January 2027 incentive fee of USD 29.30 million if earned, operator transitions, the expiry of the interest rate cap in March 2027 before the loan's March 2028 maturity, and a 2028 maturity wall that comes inside twelve months from February 2027. Over three to five years the question is whether earnings growth and asset sales bring leverage toward the issuer's stated target of 5.5x to 6.5x excluding incentive fees, which would require debt reduction: at the third-quarter run rate excluding incentive fees net leverage would be 7.28x, and reaching the top of the range would take about USD 244.75 million of net debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a reversal in senior housing during 2027: occupancy, now 83.8%, stalls or labor and insurance costs jump, or a large manager underperforms, the largest holding communities worth 30.5% of gross book value. The first operational break is segment margin, now 15.52%; each percentage point on annualised segment revenue is about USD 12.80 million of earnings, or 4.58% of trailing Adjusted EBITDAre. Financial transmission is immediate because interest is 94.27% fixed: earnings fall against unchanged interest, cover of 1.34x on cash interest tightens, free cash flow, already negative at USD 64.65 million trailing, widens, and net leverage rises from 8.20x on the adjusted measure. Even a fall back to the 2025 level of USD 266.08 million would leave net leverage at 8.62x with no debt reduction. The liquidity effect is that cash of USD 110.66 million funds the deficit and the January 2027 incentive fee, while the USD 150.00 million revolver depends on covenants that are not supplied. The refinancing effect arrives as the 2028 maturities enter their last twelve months from February 2027: replacing the notes due February 2028 at a 7.25% coupon adds USD 12.50 million a year. Management levers are deferring redevelopment, selling properties as it did in 2025 and 2026 and a distribution of only USD 9.66 million a year; they appear sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 because scheduled principal before 2028 is USD 2.55 million, but not sufficient to refinance 2028 without market access. The observable triggers are quarterly occupancy and margin, manager terminations, revolver statements and any refinancing announcement.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dhc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11, 16, 30–31, 54; calculation M3; calculation M4; calculation M5; calculation M9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Primary downside path: a margin reversal in the managed senior housing portfolio against fixed interest and negative free cash flow, which pushes the 2028 maturities into a refinancing that liquidity cannot cover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M3; calculation M4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Diversified Healthcare Trust presents an adequate but concentrated business profile supported by an improving senior housing portfolio, a maturity profile with little principal before 2028 and benign financial policy, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of about 8x to 9x, thin cover and negative free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears weak because capital spending exceeds operating cash flow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on continued margin gains, asset sales and the covenant terms of the revolver. The primary downside path is a margin reversal ahead of the 2028 maturities. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and indentures, covenant levels, peer and market data and the proxy statement. The fundamental credit synthesis is complete. Top risk: the 2028 refinancing against negative free cash flow.
